title: Alignment Cafe — Exec Prep & Quarterly OKR Draft v0.1
content:
Purpose

Quick working doc for the 'Alignment Cafe' — a lightweight facilitation format we're trying to replace the typical long exec slide deck with for this quarter. Goal: surface friction, finalize a first-pass company OKR set, and sync exec asks ahead of the all-hands. This is a workshop-style prep pack for execs + leads, not the final all-hands slides.

Quick TL;DR (for execs who scan)
- Run an 80-minute Alignment Cafe with exec + leads on Day 0 (pre-all-hands). 30m framing + metrics, 30m breakouts (signal cards + tradeoffs), 20m synth & decisions.
- Deliverable: agreed top-3 company OKRs (draft) + 6 cross-functional bets to surface in all-hands.
- Comms: short pre-read and a 10-slide all-hands output; no deep tactical docs in the all-hands.
- Open risk: capacity to absorb two big platform/infra initiatives in Q1 — need commit from infra & serving-runtime by EOD Day 2.

Agenda (Alignment Cafe runbook)
1) 0:00–0:30 — Framing + current state (owner: Sofia)
   - 6 metric snapshot (latency p95, cost per 1M tokens, uptime, adoption % of dedicated, NPS for integrations, avg eval regression rate)
   - 3 minute lightning status from each exec (2 slides max) — emphasis on one ask and one risk.
2) 0:30–1:00 — Breakouts (mixed cross-functional groups)
   - 3 breakout tables, 20m each: table A = Performance & Cost, table B = Go-to-market & PLG, table C = Security/Private & Compliance
   - Use 'signal cards' method (see below): each participant brings 2 signals, 1 bet, 1 blocker
3) 1:00–1:20 — Synthesis & decision map (owner: Marco)
   - Each table reports top 2 signals and the one recommended company-level bet. Capture in the decision ledger.
4) Follow-up (async): update the public OKR doc and push the distilled 10-slide all-hands deck.

Signal cards (facilitation notes)
- Quick template (sticky or digital): Signal = short observation (metric + trend), Evidence = pointer (dashboard/Jira), Implication = suggested action.
- Example: "p95 for hosted small-batch spikes up 30% when QPS bursts > 120/s (see metrics/dashboard p95-bursts). Implication: prioritize burst handling config or small-batch slot reservation."
- Ask participants to be concrete — signals without evidence get discarded in synth.

Proposed draft OKRs (company-level, first pass)
- OKR 1 (Reliability & SLOs): Ensure predictable inference for customers
  - KR1.1: Host p95 latency <= 200ms for 80% of production routes
  - KR1.2: Reduce production error rate by 40% vs baseline
  - KR1.3: Achieve 99.95% uptime for Hosted API across primary regions
  - Owner: Lena Müller

- OKR 2 (Cost & Efficiency): Reduce unit cost while preserving quality
  - KR2.1: Cut per-token infra cost by 18% for top 10% routes (auto-batching + cache)
  - KR2.2: Deploy two quantization profiles with no >3% quality regression on held-out evals
  - KR2.3: Increase cache hit rate for shared prefixes to 45%
  - Owner: Marco Diaz

- OKR 3 (Adoption & Platform Growth): Remove first-10-min onboarding friction
  - KR3.1: Increase integration success rate (first-30-days) from 62% to 78%
  - KR3.2: Double the number of PLG-created apps using function-calls in the demo catalog
  - KR3.3: Ship a One-Click Dedicated trial pilot with two strategic accounts
  - Owner: Aisha Khan

Notes on scope & tradeoffs (working comments)
- These OKRs aim to be visible, measurable, and cross-functional. They intentionally avoid low-level tickets (that's for product/feature OKRs to pick up).
- Trade: pushing aggressive cost KRs may conflict with latency SLO if we over-quantize; require quality guardrails from Applied ML.
- Need commitment: infra/serving-runtime must allocate a 0.5 FTE equivalent for two months to unblock KR2.1 experiment cadence.

All-hands plan (extract from Alignment Cafe deliverables)
- Format: 45 minute exec highlights + 15 minute product demo + 15 minute open Q&A. Shorten slides; each exec uses 2 slides: current state (1) + ask/decision (1).
- Slides to ship: one slide per company OKR with the 3 KRs and owners, one 'what to expect' timeline, and 6 cross-functional bets called out.
- Comms cadence: Pre-read (one-pager + metric snapshot) sent 48h before all-hands. Reminder email with 'what's at stake' 6h before.

Decision log (to capture in workshop)
- D-1: Trial the Alignment Cafe format (Decision: go ahead) — Owner: Sofia — Status: accepted
- D-2: Commit to shipping the One-Click Dedicated trial pilot as a Q1 bet — Owner: Aisha — Status: pending infra capacity check

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Too many top-level bets will diffuse focus. Mitigation: limit to 3 company OKRs + 6 bets; everything else remains team-level.
- Risk: Execs overrun breakout time -> lose synth clarity. Mitigation: assign a strict timekeeper; pre-assign roles (scribe, reporter).
- Risk: Customers confused by all-hands language (marketing vs engineering). Mitigation: product comms draft reviewed by solutions-eng before publish.

Open questions (to resolve during Cafe)
- Can infra commit to the 0.5 FTE experiment cadence for KR2.1? (asked to Blake)
- Is the One-Click Dedicated trial compliant with current Private deployment policy? (asked to Security)
- Are we comfortable with the p95 target in OKR1 given Q4 traffic patterns? (asked to SRE)

Concrete next steps (pre-all-hands timeline)
- Day -4: Collate metrics dashboard (owner: Analytics) and send pre-read (Sofia)
- Day -2: Execs submit 2 signal cards each (Marco to collect)
- Day 0: Run Alignment Cafe (facilitators: Sofia + Marco)
- Day +1: Publish final OKRs + 10-slide all-hands deck (owner: Communications)
- Day +3: Decision follow-ups — owners confirm resource commitments in the decision ledger

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep breakout groups intentionally mixed (ops + product + sales) — cross-pollination important.
- Don't over-polish the all-hands deck; we want authenticity, not perfect decks.
- If we hit pushback on cost targets, surface a 'safety valve' KR (e.g., pause heavy quant rollout) and note it in decisions.
